correctness.rationale: The two opposing support maxima give W=A+B+max(|A−B|,t|v|). Because W≥2 max(A,B) and A²+B²=1+v², equality at √2 forces v=0 and equal transverse squared coordinates, giving precisely four oriented minima. In fact 4 max(A,B)²=2[1+v²+(1−v²)|cos(2φ)|]; this uniformly localizes the event to v=O(√ε) and longitude offsets s=O(ε). Taylor expansion near a chart yields A+B=√2+v²/√2+O(s²+v⁴) and |A−B|=(1−v²)|cos(2φ)|/(A+B)=√2|s|+O(s²+|s|v²). The exact term t|v| in the maximum strengthens localization to v=O_t(ε) for fixed t>0. Haar probability is dφ dv/(4π). The fixed-t limiting rectangle has area 2√2/t; at finite t/√ε→τ the limiting section at each y is |x|≤(1−y²/√2)/√2 with |y|≤y_τ. These bounded sublevel sets have null boundaries and convergence gives both the probability and uniform conditional law, with four equal charts. Integrating yields F and the τ=0 constant; rationalization gives y_τ∼1/τ. The stated finite-τ limit and the fixed-positive-t limit are not a uniform arbitrary-path claim.
